questions.question: What tool is used to generate keyword documentation files in Robot Framework?

options.text: libdoc
robot
options.explanation: robot is for execution; libdoc generates documentation

options.text: rebot
options.explanation: rebot is for post-processing results, not documentation

options.text: docgen
options.explanation: There is no docgen command; use libdoc

questions.question: What information can be found in keyword documentation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Name of the keyword
Arguments interface with types and defaults
Return type
Documentation text describing the keyword
Source code implementation
options.explanation: Keyword documentation shows interface, not source code

questions.question: Where can you find the keyword documentation for Robot Framework Standard Libraries?

options.text: https://robotframework.org/robotframework
https://docs.robotframework.org
options.explanation: The correct URL is robotframework.org/robotframework

options.text: https://github.com/robotframework

options.text: Documentation is only available locally after installation
options.explanation: Standard library docs are available online

questions.question:
Examine this keyword documentation:

```
Should Be Equal
Arguments: first, second, msg=None, values=True, 
           ignore_case=False, strip_spaces=False, 
           collapse_spaces=False, formatter=str
```

How many mandatory arguments does this keyword have?

options.text: 2 mandatory arguments (first, second)
8 mandatory arguments (all listed)
options.explanation: Arguments with = are optional, not mandatory

options.text: 1 mandatory argument (first)
options.explanation: Both first and second lack defaults, making them mandatory

options.text: 0 mandatory arguments (all are optional)
options.explanation: Arguments without defaults are mandatory

questions.question: What distinguishes mandatory arguments from optional arguments in keyword documentation?

options.text: Mandatory arguments lack default values; optional arguments have default values shown with =
Mandatory arguments are in UPPERCASE; optional in lowercase
options.explanation: Case doesn't distinguish mandatory vs optional arguments

options.text: Mandatory arguments are marked with *; optional are not
options.explanation: * indicates varargs, not mandatory arguments

options.text: All arguments are mandatory unless marked [optional]
options.explanation: Default values (=) indicate optional arguments

questions.question: What happens if too few arguments are provided to a keyword?

options.text: The keyword call fails with an error before execution
Missing arguments are set to None automatically
options.explanation: Only optional arguments with defaults are auto-filled

options.text: The keyword executes with empty strings for missing arguments
options.explanation: Missing mandatory arguments cause immediate failure

options.text: Robot Framework prompts the user for missing values
options.explanation: RF doesn't prompt; it fails with an error

questions.question:
Analyze this test case:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Test Args
    Should Be Equal    One    One
    Should Be Equal    One    Two
    Should Be Equal    One
```

What will happen with the third keyword call?

options.text: It will fail with an error: 'expected 2 to 8 arguments, got 1'
It will pass because 'One' equals 'One'
options.explanation: Two arguments are mandatory; it fails before execution

options.text: The second argument defaults to None
options.explanation: Mandatory arguments don't have defaults

options.text: It compares 'One' with an empty string
options.explanation: Missing mandatory arguments cause failure

questions.question: How are default values represented in keyword documentation?

options.text: With an equal sign = after the argument name followed by the default value
In square brackets after the argument name
options.explanation: Square brackets are for settings, not defaults

options.text: With the keyword 'default:' before the value
options.explanation: Equal sign = is used, not 'default:'

options.text: Optional arguments are marked with ? symbol
options.explanation: Default values use =, not ?

questions.question: Which of the following are considered optional arguments in keyword documentation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Arguments with default values (arg=value)
Variable Number of Positional Arguments (*args)
Free Named Arguments (**kwargs)
Arguments without default values
options.explanation: Arguments without defaults are mandatory

questions.question: What are embedded arguments in Robot Framework?

options.text: Arguments included directly in the keyword name using ${var_name} syntax
Arguments defined inside the keyword implementation
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are in the keyword name, not implementation

options.text: Arguments passed as a single dictionary
options.explanation: This describes free named arguments, not embedded

options.text: Arguments that are optional with default values
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are mandatory, not optional

questions.question:
Analyze these keyword names with embedded arguments:

```robot
"${url}" is open
the user clicks the "${button}" button
the page title should be ${exp_title}
```

Which parts are embedded arguments? (Select all that apply)

options.text: ${url}
${button}
${exp_title}
"${button}" (including quotes)
options.explanation: Quotes are part of the keyword name for visibility, not the argument

questions.question: In Behavior-Driven keywords with embedded arguments, what happens to the Given/When/Then/And/But prefixes?

options.text: They are basically ignored by Robot Framework if a keyword matches the rest of the name
They must exactly match the keyword definition
options.explanation: RF ignores these prefixes if keyword matches the rest

options.text: They are treated as embedded arguments
options.explanation: These prefixes are ignored, not treated as arguments

options.text: They determine the execution order
options.explanation: Prefixes are for readability; execution follows definition order

questions.question: What are Positional or Named Arguments?

options.text: Arguments that can be set either by position or by name (but not both for one argument)
Arguments that must be set by position only
options.explanation: These can be set by name OR position

options.text: Arguments that must be set by name only
options.explanation: These can be set by position OR name

options.text: Arguments that require both position and name
options.explanation: Use either position or name, not both

questions.question: How are Positional or Named Arguments marked in keyword documentation?

options.text: They have no special prefix; they are the default argument kind
They are marked with a @ symbol
options.explanation: No special marking; they're the default type

options.text: They are marked with [pos/name]
options.explanation: No brackets or labels; they're the default

options.text: They are always in UPPERCASE
options.explanation: Case doesn't indicate argument type

questions.question: What is the correct order of argument kinds in a keyword interface?

options.text: Positional/Named → Variable Positional (*args) → Named-Only → Free Named (**kwargs)
Named-Only → Positional/Named → Variable Positional → Free Named
options.explanation: Positional/Named come first, Named-Only come later

options.text: All argument types can be in any order
options.explanation: There is a specific order requirement

options.text: Free Named → Variable Positional → Positional/Named → Named-Only
options.explanation: This order is backwards

questions.question: How are Variable Number of Positional Arguments (varargs) marked in keyword documentation?

options.text: With a single asterisk * before the argument name
With double asterisks ** before the argument name
options.explanation: Double ** is for free named arguments, single * for varargs

options.text: With [...] after the argument name
options.explanation: Asterisk * is used, not brackets

options.text: With the word 'varargs' in the name
options.explanation: Single asterisk * prefix is used

questions.question:
Examine this keyword documentation:

```
Run Process
Arguments: command, *arguments, **configuration
```

How should this keyword be called to execute 'ping -n 5 localhost'?

options.text: Run Process    ping    -n    5    localhost
Run Process    ping -n 5 localhost
options.explanation: This passes the entire string as command; arguments need to be separate

options.text: Run Process    command=ping    arguments=-n 5 localhost
options.explanation: Varargs (*arguments) must be positional, not named

options.text: Run Process    ping    arguments=-n    arguments=5    arguments=localhost
options.explanation: Varargs are passed positionally, not as repeated named arguments

questions.question: What happens to arguments that come after Variable Number of Positional Arguments (*varargs)?

options.text: They must be set by name only (Named-Only Arguments)
They can still be set positionally
options.explanation: After *varargs, all arguments must be named

options.text: They are not allowed
options.explanation: Named-Only Arguments are allowed after *varargs

options.text: They become part of the varargs
options.explanation: They are separate Named-Only Arguments

questions.question: How are Named-Only Arguments marked in keyword documentation?

options.text: With a label/tag symbol 🏷 before the argument name
With a single asterisk * before the argument name
options.explanation: Single * is for varargs, not named-only

options.text: With [named] after the argument name
options.explanation: Label symbol 🏷 is used, not brackets

options.text: They have no special marking
options.explanation: They are marked with a label symbol 🏷

questions.question:
Analyze this keyword documentation:

```
Get Regexp Matches
Arguments: string, pattern, *groups, 🏷flags
```

Which statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: string and pattern are Positional or Named Arguments
groups is Variable Number of Positional Arguments
flags is a Named-Only Argument
flags can be set positionally
options.explanation: Named-Only Arguments (🏷) must be set by name

questions.question: How are Free Named Arguments marked in keyword documentation?

options.text: With double asterisks ** before the argument name
With a single asterisk * before the argument name
options.explanation: Single * is for varargs; double ** for free named

options.text: With curly braces {} around the argument name
options.explanation: Double asterisks ** are used

options.text: With the word 'kwargs' in the name
options.explanation: Double asterisks ** prefix is the marker

questions.question: What do Free Named Arguments (**kwargs) collect?

options.text: All named arguments that are not explicitly defined as argument names
All positional arguments after mandatory arguments
options.explanation: Varargs (*args) collect positional; **kwargs collect named

options.text: All arguments regardless of how they're passed
options.explanation: Only unnamed named arguments are collected

options.text: Arguments marked as optional
options.explanation: They collect named arguments not in the interface

questions.question:
Consider this keyword call:

```robot
Run Process    ping    -n    5    localhost    stdout=output.txt    stderr=error.txt
```

With documentation: `Run Process: command, *arguments, **configuration`

What goes into each argument?

options.text: command='ping', arguments=['-n', '5', 'localhost'], configuration={'stdout': 'output.txt', 'stderr': 'error.txt'}
command='ping -n 5 localhost', configuration={'stdout': 'output.txt', 'stderr': 'error.txt'}
options.explanation: Positional values are split into command and arguments

options.text: All values go into arguments
options.explanation: First goes to command, middle to arguments, named to configuration

options.text: command='ping', arguments='all the rest'
options.explanation: Named arguments go to configuration, not arguments

questions.question: What happens when Robot Framework encounters an argument with a type hint and the value doesn't match?

options.text: It tries automatic type conversion; if that fails, the keyword call fails before execution
The keyword executes with the string value anyway
options.explanation: Type conversion is attempted; failure causes error

options.text: It converts to None and continues
options.explanation: Failed conversion causes an error, not None

options.text: Type hints are ignored in Robot Framework
options.explanation: Type hints are used for automatic conversion

questions.question: What is the advantage of using argument type hints?

options.text: Users get more information about expected value types
Keyword implementation can be simpler by relying on correct types
Automatic type conversion is performed
Keywords execute faster
options.explanation: Type hints improve clarity and safety, not speed

questions.question: What does a return type hint in keyword documentation indicate?

options.text: The type of value the keyword returns to the caller
Whether the keyword passed or failed
options.explanation: Return type is about the data returned, not status

options.text: The type of the last argument
options.explanation: Return type is separate from argument types

options.text: The keyword's execution time
options.explanation: Return type describes the returned data type

questions.question: If a keyword lacks a return type hint in documentation, what does that mean?

options.text: The keyword may still return values; check the documentation text
The keyword definitely returns nothing
options.explanation: Return type hints are optional and recent; keywords may still return values

options.text: The keyword is deprecated
options.explanation: Missing return type hints don't indicate deprecation

options.text: The keyword cannot be used in variable assignments
options.explanation: Keywords without type hints can still return values
